channel.title: B8ED.ie
channel.description: Satirical Irish news, sport, pop culture, politics and comedy.

item.title: LIVE: Man attempts to get a pint and get back to his seat before the second half starts
item.description: Seán left his seat at 20:41 with a tenner, a dream and no real plan. We're following every step.

item.title: We asked fans on Jones' Road to name one rule of hurling. Nobody named the same one
item.description: Our comedian went to Croke Park with a microphone and one question. Eleven fans, eleven rulebooks.

item.title: Irish mammy closes every window in the house "to keep the heat in" during 27-degree heatwave
item.description: "You'll get a chill," she told the family, who were by then mostly steam.

item.title: Unpopular opinion: the breakfast roll is not a meal, it's a cry for help
item.description: Sausage, rasher, egg, pudding, hash brown and the quiet admission that you've given up.

item.title: 21 signs you grew up in Dublin (number 14 will make you say "ah here")
item.description: You will read all 21. You won't be able to help yourself. That's the bait.

item.title: Concert-goer pays €96 for ticket, watches entire gig through the phone of the man in front
item.description: "Honestly the audio was decent," said the woman, who has seen the show only in portrait mode.

item.title: TD's constituency clinic is now just a WhatsApp group with 4,312 unread messages
item.description: "Every message is very important to me," said the TD, who has muted the group until 2027.

item.title: Government sets up committee to find out why the last committee took so long
item.description: The new committee is expected to report back in 2031, "or thereabouts".

item.title: The Budget, explained: you're getting €3 more a week, and also €5 less
item.description: Our simple guide to what it means for you, which is: not a lot, but in two different directions.

item.title: League of Ireland fan, 41, confirms that this is, once again, the year
item.description: "I said it last year and I was wrong. I said it the year before and I was wrong. That's called momentum."

item.title: 9 things you'll only ever hear in a GAA clubhouse bar
item.description: Number 6 has been said in every parish in the country since 1884.

item.title: The B8ED Comedy Night is coming to Dublin, and the open mic slots are open
item.description: A monthly live night in a Dublin bar. Big names on the bill, new acts on the open mic, and a path from there to vox pops and podcasts.

item.title: The 11 meanings of "grand", ranked from "genuinely fine" to "call an ambulance"
item.description: A guide for visitors, emigrants and anyone who's ever asked an Irish person how they are.

item.title: Open mic comedian, 26, confirms his material "works much better in the pub with the lads"
item.description: "It's a tough room," he said of a room that contained his own mother.

item.title: We ranked every way of thanking the bus driver and, frankly, you're doing it wrong
item.description: The mumbled "thanks" from the middle door does not count. It has never counted.

item.title: Bus that was "due in 4 minutes" has been due in 4 minutes since Tuesday
item.description: Passengers at the stop have formed a community, elected a chairperson and started a small vegetable patch.

item.title: Hot take: the half-time orange was the peak of Irish sport and we will not be taking questions
item.description: Protein gels, recovery shakes, ice baths. None of them ever made a seven-year-old feel like a pro.

item.title: Election poster left on lamppost since 2024 now considered a protected structure
item.description: Heritage experts say the cable ties alone are of "significant historical interest".
